name: Liang–Kleeman information flow (LKIF)
title: Which funding series move each other's uncertainty, and which way?
field: climate and ocean dynamics (causal information flow between time series)
what: Measures how much one series' past changes the uncertainty of another's next move, with size, sign, and exact zero without dynamical link.
grade: contested (sound for linear systems; independent tests thin; disputed for nonlinear systems)
pick_line: Sandwich (HAC, delta-method) inference for information flow, carrying covariance uncertainty, so short rolling and storm windows get right-sized tests.
data: Public aggregates: NY Fed fails, OFR repo, CFTC TFF, FRED VIX (weekly 2018–2025); SEC Form PF 8.27 monthly; descriptive
one: Spread moves raise fails' uncertainty and damp DVP volume's; standard tests overstate weekly links 3–13×.

picture.la: Usual tool: Granger links (Holm 5%), no size or sign
picture.lb: LKIF: signed share of uncertainty, calibrated bootstrap

findings.h: The usual tests overstate weekly links: 14–20% false alarms at 5%.
findings.t: Simulating our six weekly series from the fitted VAR(1) with one link set to zero and block-resampled residuals (fat tails and volatility clusters kept), the package's test rejects the true zero 14.5% of the time for spread → fails and 20.3% for fails → spread (400 simulations each); a circular-shift surrogate rejects 39–67% on all four edges tested; HC3 standard errors give 4.5% and 9.5%. Positioning → fails and DVP → fails are about right (3.5%, 4.3%).
findings.note: Computed. The package's z equals the lag-1 VAR t-statistic (largest gap 1.5×10⁻⁵ on our data), so this is also the Granger test's size here. The shift surrogate fails because shifting the source removes the same-week covariance that the flow is proportional to.

chart.la: False-alarm rate when the true link is zero
chart.lb: Home-field check: Liang (2021) network, printed vs ours

findings.h: Spread moves raise fails' uncertainty but damp DVP volume's.
findings.t: Six-variable LKIF, 399 weeks (2018-05-16 to 2025-12-31), conditional on volumes, positioning and VIX: spread → fails τ = +1.7% of fails' entropy budget (calibrated bootstrap p = 0.033); spread → DVP volume τ = −3.6% (p = 0.013); VIX → fails +0.5% (p = 0.076). No edge survives Holm over 30 (smallest adjusted p 0.39). VAR(BIC = 1) Granger, Holm: both spread links significant (p < 0.0001 and 0.0014), with no size or sign.
findings.note: Sign = sign of (lag coefficient × same-week covariance): positive makes the target less predictable. Under the pre-registered shift-surrogate rule three edges would have passed Holm; that rule was dropped after the size check (labelled on the On-our-data tab).

chart.title: Normalized flow τ (%) of the three strongest weekly links

findings.h: Positioning → fails: Granger says yes, information flow says about zero.
findings.t: Leveraged-fund net short → fails: VAR Granger p = 0.012 (pairwise 0.0014), but the same-week correlation is 0.02, so the flow is τ = −0.10% (bootstrap p = 0.26). Fails → spread, the direction convergent cross mapping preferred on 11-15: τ = −0.01% (p = 0.94).
findings.note: Nil-causality in action: a lagged coefficient that does not change the target's uncertainty carries no flow. The 11-17 ECA result (unwind weeks before fails spikes) is about tails, which a linear flow cannot see; the two are not in conflict.

findings.h: The spread → fails flow flips sign after mid-2024.
findings.t: τ(spread → fails) = +1.0% in 2018-05..2022-02 and +1.8% in 2022-03..2025-12 (bootstrap p 0.12 and 0.11), then −1.1% in 2024-07..2026-09 (five series without positioning; p = 0.094; +3.6% in 2022-03..2024-06). The rolling 104-week chart shows the turn.
findings.note: Not significant on its own; the timing matches the mid-2025 switch-off of the fails–spread coupling seen by CRQA on 11-14.

chart.lb: Monthly Form PF vs repo and fails

findings.h: Monthly Form PF borrowing: no flow to or from repo or fails.
findings.t: 91 months (2018-06 to 2025-12), six series: every Holm-adjusted bootstrap p = 1; the smallest Form PF ↔ market p is fails → prime-broker borrowing, 0.092. The only p < 0.05 are inside Form PF (total ↔ prime broker, 0.036 and 0.042).
findings.note: Consistent with the 11-14 and 11-17 nulls for prime-broker borrowing. The package's automatic lag choice crashed (type error), so only lag 1 was run.

chart.title: Smallest bootstrap p, Form PF ↔ market

findings.h: As a forecasting aid it does not beat ARDL or SARIMAX.
findings.t: Walk-forward one-week change in log fails, 183 weeks from 2022-07-06: ARDL own lags RMSE 0.279, + LKIF-selected parents 0.272 (−2.4%, DM p = 0.57; identical parents to Granger selection), SARIMAX(1,0,1) 0.264, random walk 0.296.
findings.note: Pre-stated bar (≥ 1% gain with DM p < 0.10) failed. Expected: the selection test is the Granger test.
